Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

play verb

a recording or a film

also play a song, play a video, put on a film, press play

modern

M-O s.v. play (a piece of music or other recording), citing Curt. 3.10.7
Quint. 11.2.1: memoriae vīs repraesentat aliquid (Lewis & Short)

repraesentō, repraesentāre, repraesentāvī, repraesentātum

verb, first conjugation

play (a recording); show (a film)

Classically to bring something before the eyes or mind, to show or exhibit it (Quint., Curt., Plin.; Lewis & Short); Morgan–Owens uses it for playing music or a film.

Other words

  • impellō, impellere, impulī, impulsum — start (a recording) by pressing play

    verb, third conjugation · also used · modern · Andresian p. 15

    Andresian labels the play button with it: classically to push or strike (Lewis & Short), as the lexicon’s push.

  • ūsurpō, ūsurpāre — play (a radio, a recording)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · modern · Traupman 361

    Classically “make use of”; the sense “play (a recording)” is Traupman’s.

Examples

  • Pelliculam iterum repraesentā, sīs.

    Play the film again, please.composed

See also film, video, television set, CD player.

SourcesLewis & Short: repraesento · Lewis & Short: impello · Lewis & Short: usurpo

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. play (a piece of music or other recording …).

Anna Andresian, Vocabula Picta (2014), p. 15.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 361.
